F-camp-camp-0045.name: Tobermory Creek rec site
F-camp-camp-0045.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a rec site (estimate).

evidence.t: Named water: easy to find on any map.
1 km or more from pavement and from private land: quieter (estimate).

flags.t: CWD (Chronic Wasting Disease) Management Zone, MU 4-23: every deer, elk and moose taken here must have its head sampled at a CWD freezer before you leave the zone (www.gov.bc.ca/CWDdropoff). Brain and spinal column (vertebrae, not the tail) may not leave the zone: leave them at the kill site or a landfill in it (synopsis pages 15, 36, 37, 99%).

Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

plan: Drive: from Cranbrook, about 162 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Official directions to Tobermory Creek rec site: At Elkford, travel north on the Elk River FSR until the 162 km road marker.
Park: 50.52318, -115.01342, the rec site. Map links below.
Hunt: 1 hunting spots within 5 km of this camp (my pick).

Legal: MU (Management Unit) 4-23, Region 4. CWD zone: deer, elk and moose heads go to a CWD freezer; brain and spine stay in the zone. No baiting in Region 4. 3 legal flags below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-04, private land 2026-09-26, closures 2026-10-03.
F-camp-camp-0045.recDirections: At Elkford, travel north on the Elk River FSR until the 162 km road marker. The recreation site is located on either side of the road.

F-grouse-drive-0071.name: 540 m E of Elkan Creek
F-grouse-drive-0071.pressureWhy: Busier: within 1 km of a paved road (estimate).
F-grouse-drive-0071.parkWhat: pull off on Elk River FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Road: Elk River FSR, 5.2 km stretch.
100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS).
4 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
2 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

Region 4: it is unlawful to feed or bait deer, elk, moose and other hoofed game, or turkeys, anywhere in the Kootenay Region (synopsis page 37, 99%). Snowmobiles may not be used for hunting in Region 4 from 1 April to 30 November (page 37, 99%).

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 4 table (pages 39 and 40), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). Pages 36 to 41 print no LEH list.
bag 2; private land only, with landowner permission

plan: Drive: from Cranbrook, about 164 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.55014, -115.06623, pull off on Elk River FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk or drive slowly: the Elk River FSR stretch, 5.2 km one way. About 105 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
